OUR LITTLE CLASSROOMS

Art Studio

Make a little mess. Make something yours.

Make a shape collage

Ages 3–825 min

Tear, arrange and layer colourful paper to make a picture that is entirely your own.

Mixing Colours

Ages 4–720–30 minutes

Predict paint mixtures, record your results, match colour cards and invent your own shade.

THE ART ROOM SHELF · 14 FLASHCARDS

Fourteen art-supply flashcards to download and print.

Every card names five real art supplies, drawn smiling and labeled for kids — from crayons and paintbrushes to clay tools, the light box and the print shop. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. The pills answer one glance: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds — and the craft-knife card wears the Ask-a-grown-up badge, because that tool stays a grown-up’s job.

THE DRAW & COLOR SHELF · 3 CARDS

Tools that make marks.

Art flashcards for the mark-makers: crayons, colored pencils and markers, ink and charcoal, and the light box that turns tracing into a game — the drawing supplies kids reach for first, drawn smiling and labeled for little artists. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

THE PAINT & MIX SHELF · 3 CARDS

Brushes, paint and a little water.

Painting flashcards for kids: the brush and palette, the water cup and sponge that run the paint session, and the canvas with its tape-and-smock setup — everything a kitchen-table studio needs. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

THE CUT, GLUE & TAPE SHELF · 4 CARDS

Paper craft, held together.

Cutting and sticking flashcards: safety scissors and glue, washi tape and craft punches, colored paper and craft sticks — and one honest rule card: the craft knife is a grown-up’s tool, closed until a grown-up picks it up. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

THE BUILD, SHAPE & PRINT SHELF · 4 CARDS

Make it stand, squish it, print it.

Building and printmaking flashcards: cardboard and foam for big ideas, clay with its rolling pin, beads and pipe cleaners for tiny fingers, and the stamp-and-ink print shop — the shelf where a craft becomes a keepsake. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

HOW TO USE THE ART CARDS

Name the tool, then hand it over.

Pick one card and name all five supplies out loud — the glue stick wants to be called by name. Then give the tool a job: crayons fill a page with color, scissors snip a zigzag, the light box traces a straight road. Print the card and tape it where the making happens, so tomorrow’s artist knows exactly where the supplies live. The studio runs on one big rule — the Ask-a-grown-up badge: everything else on this shelf is yours, and the craft knife waits.

What this room is for

The Art Studio is about making choices, not perfect pictures: tear or cut coloured paper, arrange it, layer it, then mix your own shades from red, yellow and blue washable paint. Both activities here — Make a shape collage and Mixing Colours — need nothing more than paper, a glue stick and paints you probably already have.

How one session runs

Spread a table cover first, put out the materials, and let your child lead while you narrate what you notice: “you tore that strip so small”, “the red and yellow made orange”. Every activity has a printable or on-screen sheet with drawing space, so the results can go on the wall, not in the bin.
